Cashew Chicken.

1.5 lbs boneless skinless chicken breast, cubed.

3 tbs cornstarch

1/2 tsp salt

1/2 tsp pepper

2 tbs sesame oil

1 tbs olive oil

2 tbs honey

2 cups Broccoli

1 cup red bell pepper, diced

1 cup shelled edemame

2 cloves garlic, minced

1 cup whole cashews

3 tbs soy sauce

1 tbs rice wine vinegar

1 tbs Asian Chile garlic sauce

3/4 tsp ground ginger

1 cup green onions, minced

Add chicken, cornstarch, salt and pepper to zip lock bag and shake to coat the chicken.

Add the oils and chicken to a large skillet or wok and cook for 4-5 minstrel on medium heat. Cook chicken evenly on all sides until 90% cooked.

Add Broccoli, bell peppers, garlic, and edemame. Cook 3-4 minutes or until veggies are crisp-tender and chicken is cooked.

Sauce: Add soy sauce, honey, rice wine vinegar, chili garlic sauce, and ginger to a bowl. Whisk.

Add the cashews to the skillet.

Add the sauce and stir to combine. Allow sauce to simmer on medium heat for 1-2 minutes.

Add green onions.

Stir to combine and serve.

Curried Baked Bean Soup

Incredibly tasty, cheap and quick to prepare and vegan. Easy to have the ingredients on hand.

Ingredients

  • Large Onion
  • Garlic
  • Curry Paste (or Curry Powder)
  • Tomato Paste / Puree
  • Tin of Baked Beans

Recipe

  • Thinly chop/slice the onion and fry it in a medium/large saucepan. (Pro Tip: Those onions must be brown/dark brown, but not black. Be brave!)
  • Add garlic when onions are nearly ready and fry
  • Add a tablespoon (spicy!) or two of curry paste, and fry with the onions
  • Add a tablespoon of tomatoe paste and stir
  • Add the tin of baked beans. Stir
  • Fill the baked bean can with water and add that too.
  • (Optionally add a tin of plum tomatoes, if you like)
  • Bring to boil, and simmer for 5 minutes
  • Serve with peanut butter on whole wheat toast

Terminal velocity of a spherical object through fluid flow is governed by Stoke's Law. It states that the velocity of an object of a given density, falling through a medium of given density and viscosity, will experience a buoyant drag force from the medium while under the effect of gravity.

This velocity is given by the equation:

V = 2/9 [ (density of object - density of medium) / dynamic viscosity of the medium] x g x (radius of the object)^2

Assuming standard temperature and pressure (1atm @ 20C) and knowing the height of the original World Trade Center building (417m), and knowing the properties of each medium at STP, we can calculate the velocity of a typical marble (avg density of glass 4.05 kg/m^3, radius 1cm) and the time it takes to fall. Our medium properties are thusly:

Medium Density (kg/m^3) Dynamic Viscosity (Pa*sec) Temperature (C)
Milk 1030 3 20
Corn S 1380 2.5 20
Olive O 918 84 20
Air 1.207 1.846*10^-5 20

Per 1 2 3
